We report the first detection of hot molecular cores in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC), a nearby dwarf galaxy with 0.2 solar metallicity.
Obtaining a comprehensive view of chemical compositions of hot cores at various metallicities should help understand the effect of the metallicity on the chemical evolution of protostellar sources.

We report the first detection of hot molecular cores in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC), a nearby dwarf galaxy with 0.2 solar metallicity.

This work, in conjunction with previous hot-core studies in the LMC and outer/inner Galaxy, suggests that the formation of a hot core would be a common phenomenon during high-mass star formation across the metallicity range of $0.2$–$1{\rm\:}Z_\odot$.

Compact hot-core regions are traced by SO$_2$, whose spatial extent is about $0.1{\rm\:pc}$, and the gas temperature is higher than 100 K based on the rotation diagram analysis. In contrast, CH$_3$OH, a classical hot-core tracer, is dominated by extended ($\sim$0.2–0.3${\rm\:pc}$) components in both sources, and the gas temperature is estimated to be 39$^{+8}_{-6}$ K for one source.
High-excitation SO$_2$ lines will be a useful hot-core tracer in the low-metallicity environments of the SMC and LMC.
Protostellar outflows are also detected from both sources as high-velocity components of CO.
The outflows detected in S09 is the second example of CO-traced protostellar outflows found in the SMC.

all_quotes.quote: The SO$_2$ column densities show a tight correlation with SO (correlation coefficient: 0.98), while they do not correlate with the strong-shock tracer SiO (correlation coefficient: 0.32). This would suggest that the formation of SO$_2$ in the current sample is mainly induced by the sublimation of sulfur-bearing ices, rather than sputtering by strong shocks.

The metallicity-scaled abundances of SO$_2$ in hot cores are comparable among the SMC, Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), and Galactic sources, suggesting that the chemical reactions leading to SO$_2$ formation would be regulated by elemental abundances.

As seen in the figure, the CH$_3$OH abundance shows large source-to-source variation even after corrected for the metallicity. In contrast, the metallicity-scaled abundance of SO$_2$ is relatively constant among SMC, LMC, and Galactic sources.
The SMC harbors the lowest metallicity environment (cite: Hun05; Cho18) among the Local-Group star-forming galaxies where we can detect and spatially resolve dense gas tracers.
